title: Answering atheism
tagline: Learn to give clear, kind reasons for belief in God and to hear the New Atheists fairly.
whyItMatters: Many people leave the faith because no one ever answered their honest questions about God. A calm, well-informed friend can change that.

mindset.tip: Give your reasons with gentleness and respect, and be ready to say "I do not know yet, let me look into it". (1 Peter 3:15-16)
Ask what the person means by "atheist" before you answer; many mean "I am not sure" or "I was hurt".
Listen to atheists in their own words, in debates and books, so you answer what they really hold.
Remember that arguments open doors, but people are won by trust and by a life that shows the faith is good (CCC 2123-2128, 856).

levels.title: Foundations
levels.goal: Know what atheism claims and what reason can say about God.

steps.why: Start with the app's own short answer to "Does God exist?".
Learn what "atheist" really means and where the burden of proof lies.
See what kind of proof is possible for God.
Hear a bishop explain the kind of evidence we should expect.
Short catechism lesson on ways to know God by reason.
Why faith is both reasonable and free.
A plain definition of what Christians mean by creation.

steps.prompt: If a friend said, "I just don't see any reason to believe in God," what is the first question you would ask?

levels.title: Making the case
levels.goal: Be able to state three or four good arguments for God in plain words.

steps.why: Read the five ways in Aquinas's own words.
See a modern defense of the argument from a first cause.
Understand the fine-tuning argument.
Try the argument from desire.
Watch the same argument in a short video.
Hear why Aquinas has not been refuted.
What the Church means by creation out of nothing.
Tertullian says even ordinary people know God from the soul itself.

levels.title: Objections and replies
levels.goal: Meet the strongest objections, including from the New Atheists, and answer them fairly.

steps.why: Answer "Who made God?" and "Is this a personal God?".
Use the moral argument: right and wrong point beyond us.
The app's answer to the hardest objection.
Does science make God unnecessary?
Read a neutral account of what atheists and agnostics hold.
Watch a Catholic and an atheist debate in their own words.
Watch a bishop take the hardest questions from an atheist.
Read what the Church says about atheism and its causes (nos. 19-21).
Read about a famous debate with Richard Dawkins.

levels.title: Going deeper
levels.goal: Read the classic sources and the best book-length cases.

steps.why: A full book that goes through the main arguments with charity.
Study five classical proofs closely.
Read Aquinas on God written for non-Christians.
Follow the detailed fine-tuning case and the multiverse reply.
Read the Church's teaching on how faith and reason fit together.
An early Christian dialogue with an unbeliever (the Octavius).
Origen answers a pagan critic, line by line (Book 1).
Newman on how real people come to certain belief.
Explore science-based arguments for God.
